explain.say: When wind blows past a thin wire or twig, the air cannot flow smoothly around it. Little whirlpools of air peel off behind, first one side, then the other.

explain.say: Each swirl gives the surrounding air a small push. When they peel off at a steady rate, those pushes make a sound wave with a steady pitch, called an Aeolian tone.

faq.a: Vortex shedding is when a fluid flowing past an object sheds swirling whirlpools, called vortices, from alternate sides. The regular shedding can make an object vibrate and produce a tone.
asks: Why does air swirl behind things?

faq.q: Why does wind whistle through wires?
faq.a: Wind flowing past a wire sheds swirls of air from side to side at a regular rate. The pushes from these swirls make a steady note called an Aeolian tone.
asks: Why do power lines hum in the wind?

faq.q: Why does stronger wind whistle higher?
faq.a: Faster wind makes the swirls peel off more often each second. More pushes per second means a higher frequency, so the pitch rises.
asks: Why does the whistle change pitch?
Why does wind sound higher in a gale?

faq.a: An Aeolian harp is a stringed instrument played by the wind, not by a person. Wind blowing across the strings makes them sing with Aeolian tones. It is named after Aeolus, the Greek god of the winds.

faq.q: Why does the wind howl around houses?
faq.a: Wind blowing across gaps, chimneys and openings makes the air inside them resonate, like blowing across the top of a bottle. Gusts change the strength, so the howl rises and falls.
asks: Why does a chimney moan in the wind?

facts: Tones made by wind flowing past wires and twigs are called Aeolian tones, after Aeolus, Greek god of the winds.
Czech physicist Vincenz Strouhal studied the tones made by wires in moving air in 1878; their pitch rises with wind speed and falls with wire thickness.

quiz.say: In the same wind, a thin wire and a thick cable both whistle. Which makes the higher note?
quiz.why: Swirls peel off a thin wire more often each second, so it makes a higher-pitched tone.

wrong.1: A thick cable sheds swirls less often, giving a lower note.
wrong.2: The pitch depends on the thickness, so they differ.
